tasks.title: Describing a wait status
tasks.statement: A parent got a status from wait/waitpid and has to write it to a log in plain words. Write describe_status(status, buf, n) using only the macros WIFEXITED, WEXITSTATUS, WIFSIGNALED, WTERMSIG, WCOREDUMP, WIFSTOPPED, WSTOPSIG, WIFCONTINUED (shifts and masks such as 0x7f or >> 8 are counted as a violation by the driver). Format: "exited with N", "killed by signal N", "killed by signal N (core dumped)", "stopped by signal N", "continued", otherwise "unknown status". The string goes into buf of size n through snprintf (it is truncated when there is no room), and the function returns the length of the resulting string. The driver spawns real children: ones that exit with codes 0, 3 and 263 (the parent gets only the low byte), ones killed by signals, one stopped and then continued, and it builds a core-dump status by hand.
tasks.hint: Test the macros in order: WIFEXITED, WIFSIGNALED, WIFSTOPPED, WIFCONTINUED. Return the length with strlen(buf), not the value of snprintf: that one counts the untruncated string.

tasks.title: A two-program pipeline
tasks.statement: Implement with fork, pipe, dup2 and execvp what a shell does for "left | right". The function run_pipeline(left, right, out, cap) creates two pipes (one between the programs, one to bring the output back to the parent), spawns two children, puts the ends onto descriptors 0 and 1, closes all spare ends and starts the programs. The parent reads the output of right to end-of-file (out holds at most cap-1 bytes, the rest is read and discarded, the string is NUL-terminated), waits for both children and returns the exit code of right, 128 + the signal number if right was killed, or -1 if pipe/fork fails. A failed exec gives code 127 in the child. The driver runs sort, tr, wc, nonexistent commands, large output (seq with 20,000 lines), truncated output and a process killed by a signal, then checks that no children and no leaked descriptors remain. system() and popen() are forbidden. If you forget to close the write end in the parent, the test hangs on wc: the reader never gets EOF.
tasks.hint: In a child: dup2 first, then close all four ends, then execvp, and _exit(127) after it. In the parent close a[0], a[1], b[1] before reading from b[0].

tasks.title: What survives exec
tasks.statement: A descriptor without FD_CLOEXEC is handed to the new program after exec; with the flag it is closed. Write four functions. set_cloexec(fd, on) reads the descriptor flags with fcntl(F_GETFD), turns FD_CLOEXEC on or off and writes them back with F_SETFD; 0 on success, -1 on failure (errno stays from fcntl, for a bad fd it is EBADF). is_cloexec(fd) returns 1, 0 or -1. pipe_cloexec(fds) creates a pipe whose two ends have the flag from the start, with a single pipe2 call (so no window is left between pipe and fcntl for someone else's fork+exec in another thread; the driver checks the flags of both ends and that neither is visible after exec). spawn_with_fd(argv, fd) does fork and execv(argv[0], argv); in the child, before exec, clear the flag of fd so exactly that descriptor survives the exec while all others that have the flag are closed. The parent waits for the child and returns its exit code (127 if exec failed). The flag of fd in the parent stays as it was: the child has its own descriptor table. The driver starts a real shell and checks through /proc/self/fd which descriptors it sees.
tasks.hint: set_cloexec: fl = fcntl(fd, F_GETFD); fl |= FD_CLOEXEC or fl &= ~FD_CLOEXEC; fcntl(fd, F_SETFD, fl). pipe2 needs #define _GNU_SOURCE before the includes; it is already in the starter.

tasks.title: A sum computed by child processes
tasks.statement: Shared memory between related processes is an mmap with MAP_SHARED | MAP_ANONYMOUS made before fork. Implement parallel_sum(v, n, workers): create such a mapping for workers long values, spawn workers children (child i sums the slice [i*n/workers, (i+1)*n/workers) and stores the sum in cell i, then _exit(0)), wait for all children (wait), add up the cells, unmap with munmap and return the total. If workers < 1, mmap or fork fails, or some child did not end with code 0, return -1 (children already started still have to be waited for). Threads are forbidden. The driver checks the sums for various n and workers (including workers larger than n and n = 0), that the input array is untouched, that no unreaped children remain, and that the number of mappings of the process is back to what it was. A MAP_PRIVATE variant or a plain array returns zeros: the children write into their own copies.
tasks.hint: Compute the slice bounds in long so that i*n cannot overflow int. Children use _exit, not exit: they have no business with the parent's stdio buffers.

tasks.title: A file through mmap
tasks.statement: Three functions that work with a file only through mmap (calls to read, pread and fopen are counted as a violation by the driver). count_byte(path, c) maps the file PROT_READ | MAP_PRIVATE and counts occurrences of byte c; an empty file gives 0 without calling mmap (length 0 is an EINVAL error for mmap), a missing file gives -1. overwrite_at(path, off, s) opens the file O_RDWR, maps it MAP_SHARED, copies s (without the NUL) at offset off, calls msync(MS_SYNC) and unmaps; if off + strlen(s) goes past the file size, change nothing and return -1 (a write beyond the end through the mapping would raise SIGBUS or not change the file); 0 on success. byte_at(path, off) returns the byte at offset off, mapping only one page: the mmap offset must be rounded down to a multiple of sysconf(_SC_PAGE_SIZE), otherwise EINVAL. If off is past the end of the file, return -1. The driver writes a file of 200000 bytes and checks offsets before and after a page boundary and a write that crosses a boundary.
tasks.hint: For byte_at: base = off - off % page; the mapping length is (off - base) + 1; the byte is at m[off - base]. Take the file size from fstat.

tasks.title: An ioctl request number by hand
tasks.statement: Take a request number apart the way strace or an attentive reader of a header does. Write ioc_encode(dir, type, nr, size), which builds the number with shifts and masks (nr in bits 0-7, type in 8-15, size in 16-29, dir in 30-31; this layout is shared by x86, ARM and RISC-V, while powerpc and some other architectures differ), ioc_decode(req, &dir, &type, &nr, &size) for the reverse, and ioc_macro(dir), which names the macro: 0 is "_IO", 1 is "_IOW", 2 is "_IOR", 3 is "_IOWR" (W and R are counted from the user's side: _IOW means the kernel reads the argument). The macros _IOC*, _IO, _IOR, _IOW, _IOWR must not be used; the driver itself compares your numbers with them. It decodes real KVM requests (KVM_GET_API_VERSION, KVM_CREATE_VM, KVM_SET_USER_MEMORY_REGION, KVM_RUN and others), two made-up requests and two old terminal requests (FIONREAD, TIOCGWINSZ) whose size and direction are not encoded.
tasks.hint: Build the value in an unsigned long: dir=3 is shifted into the top bits of a 32-bit number. Mask the size with 0x3fff and the direction with 3.

tasks.title: Driving a device through ioctl
tasks.statement: The device /dev/ticker is a counter controlled only by ioctl requests; the sandbox has none, so the driver replaces open, ioctl and close with a model, and you write real code with real calls (the requests are defined in the starter and must not be changed). ticker_run(path, step, n) opens path, checks the interface version with TICK_GET_VERSION (2 is required, otherwise the error is EPROTO), sets the step with TICK_SET_STEP, calls TICK_ADVANCE n times (no argument) and returns the value of TICK_GET_TOTAL. On any failure return -errno of the cause, after closing the descriptor. A subtlety: a successful close is allowed to leave anything in errno (the model sets EIO), so errno has to be saved before closing. The model answers like a kernel: EBUSY on a busy device, EINVAL for a step of 0 or less, ENOENT for an unknown path, and it reports version 1 for /dev/ticker-old. The driver prints the result and how many times the counter was opened, closed and advanced: a descriptor leak shows at once.
tasks.hint: Keep a variable err: in the failure branch set err = errno right after the failed call, call close(fd) once at the end, then return err ? -err : total.

tasks.title: FIONREAD and TIOCGWINSZ
tasks.statement: Two real ioctl commands that appear in programs all the time. pending_bytes(fd) asks a pipe through FIONREAD (the argument is a pointer to an int) how many bytes can already be read; the number or -errno. read_available(fd, buf, cap) reads at most cap bytes but only what is ready: if the pipe is empty, it returns 0 and does not call a blocking read (otherwise the test would hang on an empty pipe); the number of bytes read or -errno. terminal_width(fd) asks the width of a terminal through TIOCGWINSZ (struct winsize, field ws_col): if fd is not a terminal (error ENOTTY) or the width is 0, it returns 80, and any other error is -errno. The driver uses a real pipe, the real /dev/null, a bad descriptor and a "terminal" of 24 by 132 faked through --wrap=ioctl (plus one with a zero width).
tasks.hint: pending_bytes: int n; ioctl(fd, FIONREAD, &n). Save errno right after the ioctl, before you call anything else.

tasks.title: A process tree from strace -f
tasks.statement: text is the output of strace -f ... for a command, root is the pid of its main process. The main process's lines come without a prefix, the others start with "[pid N]" (the number may be padded with spaces). Write a function fork_tree(text, root): return a list of tuples (pid, parent, exec, end), sorted by pid, for the main process and every process that appears in the text. parent is the creator's pid (None for the main process); it is known from the clone, clone3, fork or vfork call that returned this pid as a positive number (`= 3001`; a result of -1 creates nobody). exec is the path of the last SUCCESSFUL (result 0) execve or execveat call (for execveat the path is the second argument after AT_FDCWD), otherwise None; failed attempts (ENOENT and the like) do not count. end is "exit N" for the line "+++ exited with N +++" and "signal NAME" for "+++ killed by NAME ... +++" (ignore the core dump note), otherwise None. Calls can be split: "... <unfinished ...>" on one line and "<... name resumed>...) = N" on another (with the prefix of the same process, lines of other processes may come between them); the path of execve is visible only in the first half, the result only in the second. Ignore "--- SIGCHLD ... ---" lines and other system calls.
tasks.hint: For each line find the process (the prefix or root) and the body. For a split call remember the name and path per pid; on the resumed line take them back. The result is the last ") = number" in the line.

tasks.title: Parents that never call wait
tasks.statement: text is the output of ps -eo pid,ppid,stat,args (or with a COMMAND header instead of ARGS). Columns are separated by spaces; the first is the pid, the second the ppid, the third the state, the rest of the line is the command (it may contain spaces). A zombie is a process whose state starts with Z (Z, Z+, Zl and so on). Write a function find_zombies(text): return a list of tuples (ppid, [zombie pids in ascending order], the parent's command), one per parent that has at least one zombie, sorted by ppid. Take the parent's command from its own line in the text; if the parent is not in the text, it is "?". Skip lines that do not start with two numbers (the header).
tasks.hint: line.split(None, 3) gives pid, ppid, state and the rest as the command. Build a dictionary "ppid -> list of zombies" and a dictionary "pid -> command".
